summary.text: A 63-year-old woman with no history of smoking presented with progressively decreased vision in the left eye over one month. Visual acuity was 6/12 in the right eye and 6/60 in the left, with dilated episcleral vessels, an amelanotic choroidal mass and exudative retinal detachment in the left eye, while the right eye showed no abnormalities.

Ultrasonography showed a hyperechoic subretinal mass about 6.61 mm thick, and angiography showed hypofluorescence with two small spots near the fovea. Serologies were negative, chest radiography showed a left upper lobe opacity, and PET/CT showed uptake in the left eye, left upper lung, mediastinum, liver and bone. CT found a 2.8-cm left upper lobe tumor with nodal metastasis; biopsy showed giant and spindle cells positive for vimentin and cytokeratin.

The final diagnosis was stage 4 pleomorphic carcinoma of the lung with nodal and multiple distant metastases, with the choroidal metastasis highly likely but not biopsy-confirmed. She was transferred to oncology and informed of her cancer; radiotherapy with systemic therapy was suggested but not implemented because she chose hospice care at home, and she died 4 months after the diagnosis.
